cohort: The study cohort included 256 women undergoing forceps delivery for live, singleton, term cephalic pregnancies at Showa Medical University Hospital between April 2021 and September 2024.
finding: Several intrapartum ultrasound parameters, most notably Head Direction during pushing, were significantly associated with and predictive of obstetric anal sphincter injury in forceps deliveries.
mod_finding: Intrapartum ultrasound, particularly Head Direction during pushing, is a valuable predictor of obstetric anal sphincter injury in forceps deliveries, with a cut-off value of 36 degrees for identifying higher risk.
